name: Magus
caption: A former EWA Television Champion on a four-match losing streak in October 1996, who cut two promos on three rivals ahead of a four-way match at Sunday Night RARE.

tenures.source: /promotions/ewa-rspwf/archive/ewa-sunday-night-rare-23-1996-06-16.html (the Television title match, with Magus the champion); the post of 20 October 1996 (/promotions/rspwf/archive/if-you-think-you-are-the-best-rper-then-read-this-1996-10-20.html)

identity.note: Shares a bare ring name with four held Magus records at other federations. This Magus is tied to the EWA by its own pages: the Sunday Night RARE of 16 June 1996 names him the Television champion, and the October 1996 post has him as a former EWA Television champion on a losing streak ahead of a Sunday at RARE. No operator, roster or text connects him to the others; filed distinct.

name: "Idolizer" Trace Michaels
caption: The self-declared biggest fan of "Dreamlover" Trey Porter, who hosted the first and only ITM Show for the EWA in October 1996 and was slapped and clotheslined by his own guest, Gary Grayson.

tenures.source: /promotions/rspwf/archive/idolizer-trace-michaels-roleplay-1996-10-21.html (his own talk show for "EWA fans", a Halloween Hell match booked against Sir Olympia, and his account of wrestling the EWA's wrestlers)

identity.note: Shares the billing "Idolizer" Trace Michaels with idolizer-trace-michaels-rspwf, a 2003 RSPWF Top 200 entry tagged I-Slash. Name plus moniker is a lead, never a receipt on its own, and nothing ties the 1996 EWA host to a 2003 I-Slash wrestler: filed distinct, reopenable on a document naming both. trace-michaels-bawf-1997b ("Dreamlover" Trace Michaels, BAWF, Feb 1998) is a further lead: the host idolised "Dreamlover" Trey Porter, but a different moniker is no receipt either.

name: Stixx
caption: A WEW World champion from V-Town, Washington who had just signed with the EWA when he guested on the ITM Show in October 1996, wrecked the set and promised his Stixx-Plex to the host.

tenures.source: /promotions/rspwf/archive/idolizer-trace-michaels-roleplay-1996-10-21.html (introduced as "a newcomer to the EWA" who "just signed with the EWA" after the WEW closed)

name: Brian Nelson
caption: The EWA's lead commentator in the summer of 1996, calling Wednesday WAR and the Offensive Dreams and Extreme Realization pay-per-views beside J.R. Neubs; in May 1997 he called the main event of PCW's Spring Showdown.
